facts.fact: Badami is Jassi's old bell-goat, too old for crossings, left in the salt-house pen. Jassi carries her kid-days bell on a thong at his collar; she is to retire with him to his sister's orchard of forty apricot trees.
facts.why: the beat requires Badami and her bell (C25) to be carried by Jassi on the crossing.

facts.fact: Meera takes Badami's small dented brass kid-bell from Jassi's fist and keeps it buttoned in her coat with Kiran's note.
Rohan has two or three cracked ribs on his left side and cannot raise his left arm above the shoulder.
facts.why: beat says ribs cracked; the arm restriction is a small detail.

facts.fact: Of the five pack goats, Pomegranate and Auntie are dug out dead; the other three are never found. All the wardens' probes and tent poles are lost or left behind.
facts.why: the slide has to account for the goats and gear.

facts.fact: Rohan believes Varun was buried in the slide and is dead; Meera heard an iron ring before the first crack but has not interpreted it.
facts.why: Varun's tracks are buried per beat; C05 is planted without exposing the scheme.

facts.fact: Meera gave Rohan odds: about one in four the gully slides, one in three the face cornice; Varun chose the gully as the lesser risk.
facts.why: supports technique 6 and ties to Varun's route choice.
